evidence.title: Women in UK arts feel they do not have equal opportunities for roles, says report

occurrences.checkable_against: Arts Council England taskforce terms of reference and subsequent recommendations
occurrences.quote_span: An Arts Council England spokesperson said the group would “consider the challenges women face around issues such as glass ceilings, harassment and caring responsibilities”, with a view to identifying good practice and interventions that support women at work.
occurrences.speaker: Arts Council England spokesperson
occurrences.subject: Women in the Arts survey of UK arts professionals

occurrences.checkable_against: Women in the Arts project records and partnership agreements
occurrences.quote_span: The findings are from a survey undertaken as part of a five-year research project by Women in the Arts, run in partnership with the Writers’ Guild of Great Britain, Equity, WOW, Sphinx Theatre, ERA 50:50 and the Women in Theatre Lab.
occurrences.speaker: outlet's own
occurrences.subject: Women in the Arts survey of UK arts professionals

occurrences.checkable_against: Women in the Arts survey responses and arts-sector talent/commissioning records
occurrences.quote_span: “There seems to be absolutely no celebration of experienced, seasoned, insightful, adult, et cetera. It’s always fresh. As if anything that isn’t fresh is mouldy,” she said.

occurrences.subject: Women in the Arts survey of UK arts professionals

occurrences.checkable_against: Women in the Arts report and Maureen Beattie’s statement

occurrences.subject: Women in the Arts survey of UK arts professionals

occurrences.checkable_against: Women in the Arts survey responses and commissioning records
occurrences.quote_span: One person working in arts marketing said there was a prevalent idea that only young people truly understood the online world, while a writer felt that the stories of older women were seldom commissioned.
occurrences.speaker: unnamed arts-marketing worker and unnamed writer survey participants
occurrences.subject: Women in the Arts survey of UK arts professionals

occurrences.checkable_against: Women in the Arts report recommendations
occurrences.quote_span: The report called for more targeted work to address gender discrimination, including more funding to address the problem, representation targets – potentially mirroring those in Australia, where these are required in funding applications – and leadership programmes, as well as algorithmic audits to minimise bias.
occurrences.speaker: Women in the Arts report
occurrences.subject: Women in the Arts survey of UK arts professionals

figure.unit: times as many roles for male colleagues

occurrences.quote_span: another female actor said: “There are twice as many roles for my male colleagues as there are for me. There are even fewer roles for actresses over 50.”

occurrences.subject: Women in the Arts survey of UK arts professionals

occurrences.checkable_against: Women in the Arts survey responses and casting records
occurrences.quote_span: “Often younger actresses are cast to play opposite men who are older for parts that are supposed to be the same age,” said one actor.

occurrences.quote_span: The research said that gender discrimination and ageism were being exacerbated by the use of AI in hiring, which can penalise women for taking career breaks for caring responsibilities, or reinforce historical biases.
